record.paper_title: Spectral analysis for a class of integral-difference operators: known facts, new results, and open problems
record.original_question: Let phi be a nonnegative integrable equilibrium distribution with infinite support for the integral-difference operator K_phi on L2(R, dx). In this setting phi cannot be uniformly separated from zero on all of R, the compact-support resolvent-comparison method is unavailable, and the constant-equilibrium reference operator K0 is only defined on finite intervals because the corresponding integrals diverge on infinite intervals. Which alternative reference operator should be chosen and developed for spectral analysis of K_phi when phi has infinite support?

evidence.quote: as ϕ(x) is nonnegative and integrable, it cannot simultaneously have an infinite support and be uniformly separated from zero on the whole axis R.
Another difficulty for functions ϕ(x) with infinite support is due to the fact that in this case, we have no relation similar to (3.51).
reference operator with constant equilibrium distribution function like K0 can be defined only for finite intervals, otherwise, the corresponding integrals diverge.
This brings an idea that for ϕ(x) with infinite support, another reference operator should be chosen and investigated. However, no results in this direction are yet known.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\varphi:\mathbb{R}\to[0,\infty)$ be a nonnegative integrable function (an "equilibrium distribution") with $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\varphi(x)\,dx<\infty$ and with infinite support, i.e.\ the set $\{x\in\mathbb{R}:\varphi(x)>0\}$ is unbounded. Consider the integral-difference operator $K_\varphi$ acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R},dx)$ by
$$(K_\varphi f)(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}} k(x-y)\,\sqrt{\varphi(x)\varphi(y)}\,f(y)\,dy,$$
where $k$ is a fixed even, real-valued kernel (the "difference" kernel) such that $K_\varphi$ defines a bounded self-adjoint operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R},dx)$.

For the case when $\varphi$ has compact support, spectral information about $K_\varphi$ can be obtained by comparing its resolvent with that of the "constant-equilibrium" reference operator
$$(K_0 f)(x)=c\int_{I} k(x-y)\,f(y)\,dy,\qquad x\in I,$$
acting on $L^2(I,dx)$ for a finite interval $I\subset\mathbb{R}$ with $c>0$ constant on $I$. When $\varphi$ has infinite support, two obstructions arise:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\varphi$ cannot simultaneously be integrable and uniformly bounded away from zero on $\mathbb{R}$, so the compact-support resolvent-comparison method does not apply;
\item the constant-equilibrium reference operator $K_0$ cannot be defined on all of $\mathbb{R}$ because the corresponding integrals diverge.
\end{enumerate}

Problem: Construct an alternative reference operator $K_{\mathrm{ref}}$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R},dx)$, adapted to equilibrium distributions $\varphi$ with infinite support, that is (i) explicitly definable on all of $\mathbb{R}$ without divergence, (ii) amenable to resolvent or related comparison with $K_\varphi$, and (iii) yields effective spectral information (essential spectrum, discrete spectrum, asymptotics of eigenvalues) for $K_\varphi$. Develop the corresponding spectral analysis of $K_\varphi$ via this reference operator.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem: no alternative reference operator and no corresponding spectral analysis for integral-difference operators $K_\varphi$ with equilibrium distribution of infinite support are known. A brief web search did not surface any subsequent work resolving this question, so the problem appears to remain open.
